Directory Description: 1400 Bar & Grill is a casual gastropub at the corner of Webster Street and Central Avenue in Alameda's West End. It fills the ground floor of the historic Croll Building, built in 1879. The building once housed Croll's Gardens and Hotel, where boxing greats such as James J. Corbett and Jack Johnson trained around the turn of the 20th century. It is now a California Historical Landmark, and the restaurant keeps its stained glass, etched windows and carved wooden bar. The kitchen serves pub fare drawn from a range of culinary traditions, with daily specials and pizza. Takeout and delivery are available.
Verify Before Publishing: No official website or verified hours found. Also listed as '1400 Bar & Grill and Pizza'.

Directory Description: A-Town Pizza and Kabob House has been a neighborhood fixture on Blanding Avenue since the late 1980s. It serves two cuisines: American-style gourmet pizza on dough made fresh every day, and Afghan kabobs char-broiled after marinating in house seasoning. Pizza favorites include the loaded A-Town Special and a gourmet veggie pie. On the kabob side there are chopan (lamb chop), tekah (beef) and chicken kabobs. Halal pizzas, pastas and kabobs make it a good choice for families with a range of dietary needs. The shop is open seven days a week for dine-in, pickup and delivery.

Abigail's Moroccan Cuisine is a family-run restaurant on Ballena Isle with views over San Francisco Bay. Jonathan and Fatima Belkhalfia opened it in 2010 and named it after their daughter. The menu offers home-style Moroccan cooking, including kefta sandwiches, harira and lentil soups, saffron rice plates, Moroccan salads, and slow-cooked tagines such as lamb with almonds and dried plums or chicken with green olives and preserved lemon. Saturday dinners are a highlight, with belly dancing entertainment. Guests may bring their own wine. Lunch is served most days and dinner on weekends.
Verify Before Publishing: CONFIRM STILL OPEN: its website (abigailsalameda.com) now redirects to an unrelated site, though Yelp/OpenTable were updated in 2026. Phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Alameda Brewing is a family-owned craft brewery and taproom on Park Street in downtown Alameda. Founder Bill Phua and his son Vince run it. It opened as Alameda Island Brewing Company and, in 2024, took back the name it had always intended, with a new nautical rope "A" logo and a refreshed taproom. The rotating lineup runs from West Coast and hazy IPAs to a Czech pilsner, German lager, hefeweizen and a playful ube ale, plus hard seltzer and non-alcoholic options. There is no kitchen, but guests may bring food or order from neighboring restaurants on the shared patio. Kids with adults and leashed dogs are welcome, and the calendar includes live music, trivia and comedy.
Verify Before Publishing: Formerly Alameda Island Brewing Co. (renamed 2024). Phone not confirmed; hours vary by season.

Directory Description: Alameda Cinema Grill is a neighborhood restaurant and bar inside the Alameda Theatres Cineplex on Central Avenue. Its "backstage pass" corridor connects directly to the cinema, so guests can have dinner and then take their food and drinks into the movie. The kitchen serves eclectic comfort food. The bar pours craft cocktails inspired by Hollywood's Golden Age, alongside beer and wine. Weekend brunch, regular live music, and Wednesday comedy and karaoke nights make it a lively spot even without a film. For celebrations, the restaurant offers party packages, including options that pair a private theater rental with a full meal.

Alley & Vine is a New American restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. It serves seasonal dishes, freshly baked breads and handcrafted cocktails in a warm neighborhood setting. The menu leans toward seafood and chophouse favorites such as king salmon, branzino, seafood risotto, lamb chops and filet mignon, with house focaccia on the side. Daytime diners will find dishes like ham benedict. The restaurant is open daily from late morning through dinner, takes reservations, and handles private parties and catering.

Ark Chinese Restaurant is a casual Park Street spot best known for hand-pulled noodles, which are made fresh in the kitchen and served in hearty noodle soups and lo mein dishes. The broad menu of traditional Chinese dishes covers beef, chicken, pork and vegetarian options, along with favorites like xiao long bao and golden braised egg tofu. Big round tables make it a natural choice for family dinners and group meals, and it is also a regular weekday lunch stop. Takeout and delivery are available.
Verify Before Publishing: Three websites exist (arkalameda.com, arkchinese.com, arkatpark.com); official one unclear.

Directory Description: Asena Restaurant has served Mediterranean cooking on Santa Clara Avenue in downtown Alameda since 1996. Owners Mustafa Yildirim and Muhittin Arpaci grew up in kitchens where their mothers cured olives and baked bread, and they bring that from-scratch approach to Asena. The kitchen bakes its own bread, rolls fresh pasta, cures salmon and preserves lemons in house. It sources fresh, seasonal, local and organic ingredients wherever possible. Asena is open for dinner Monday through Saturday, offers catering, and has long supported Alameda schools and charities.

Bhan Mae Vane is a modern Lao and Thai restaurant on Webster Street in Alameda's West End, run by sisters Bebe Lach, the chef, and Thip Tran. Their mother's recipes inspire the menu, which updates traditional dishes with local, seasonal ingredients. The cooking features the bold spice, funk and earthy bitterness at the heart of Lao and Thai food, in dishes like crispy pork belly, slow-simmered red curry, and tapioca dumplings filled with pork and peanuts. The dining room is casual and lively, well suited to big groups. Lunch and dinner are served Tuesday through Sunday, and takeout is available.

Burma Superstar brings Burmese cooking to Park Street in downtown Alameda, where it has served the neighborhood since 2008 as part of a Bay Area brand dating to 1992. The kitchen draws on a cuisine shaped by India, China, Laos and Thailand. Its best-known dish is the tea leaf salad of fermented tea leaves, vegetables and crunchy nuts. Samusa soup, flaky platha flatbread, khao swè curry noodles and beef curry are also favorites. The warm, neighborhood-style dining room suits first-time visitors and family dinners alike. Reservations are available, and the restaurant also offers online pickup ordering, catering and gift cards. Open daily for lunch and dinner.

C'era Una Volta ("once upon a time") has been cooking Tuscan-style Italian food in Alameda since 2004. Chef Rutilio "Rudy" Fanetti-Durán and Cheryl Principato founded it. Today the kitchen operates inside the SoFive Soccer Club at Alameda Point, focusing on carryout, delivery and catering, with indoor and outdoor seating. The menu features house-made pasta, pizza and salads, seasonal dishes, vegetarian and vegan options, and weekly Tuesday specials. It also caters corporate events and parties and delivers to nearby wineries. Honors include repeated recognition from the Accademia Italiana della Cucina and a Best of Alameda 2025 award.
Verify Before Publishing: Now operates inside SoFive Soccer Club, mainly carryout/delivery/catering; older listings still describe full-service dinners.

Directory Description: Cafe Jolie is a French-inspired neighborhood restaurant on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. It focuses on organic, seasonal cooking led by Executive Chef Joann Guitarte. Diners know it for breakfast and weekend brunch, and the menu also includes French-American plates such as steak frites, Dungeness crab cocktail and beignets. Beer and wine are served, gluten-free options are available, and there is patio seating outdoors. Live jazz on Friday and Saturday evenings adds to the relaxed, welcoming feel. Takeout is available, and a public parking lot sits next door.
Verify Before Publishing: Hours conflict between listings (brunch-only vs. Thu–Sat dinner); website would not load.

Directory Description: Calafia Taqueria has served fresh, traditional Mexican food on Webster Street in Alameda's West End for more than two decades. The menu is built around taqueria staples with a wide choice of fillings: carne asada, pollo asado, carnitas, chile verde, lengua, al pastor, shredded chicken, fish and shrimp. Guests can eat in, order ahead online for pickup, or use the free parking next to the restaurant. Calafia also caters parties and community events around the island, and its patio is available to rent for gatherings.

Casa Revolución Taqueria serves fresh, fairly priced Mexican food on Santa Clara Avenue near downtown Alameda. The menu covers breakfast, lunch and dinner. Corn tortillas are made by hand, and the salsa bar lets diners dress their tacos as they like. Birria is a house specialty, and tacos anchor the menu. The taqueria offers dine-in, takeout and online ordering for pickup or delivery, and it can cater gatherings with buffet-style spreads. With early weekend openings, it works for a morning breakfast burrito as well as an evening taco run.
Verify Before Publishing: Phone conflict (also 510-217-8959, 510-422-4089); one directory lists 2520 Santa Clara. Owners not found.

Directory Description: Ceron Kitchen opened on Webster Street in Alameda's West End in October 2021. Owner Vicente Ceron, who founded it with Executive Chef Juan Jaquez, had long dreamed of opening a restaurant. Chef Jaquez cooks New American food with careful plating and deep flavors. Dishes include New Zealand lamb, duck breast, seafood pasta, ribeye with bleu cheese and clam chowder, alongside craft cocktails. Complimentary pastries often close the meal. The restaurant is open daily for lunch and dinner, takes reservations, and hosts private parties and catering. It received an OpenTable Diners' Choice award in 2025, and free parking is available nearby.

Cholita Linda brings Latin street and comfort food to Park Street in downtown Alameda. It is the second location of the Oakland favorite that chef Vanessa Chavez and her husband Murat Sozeri grew from popular farmers market stands. Chavez's Peruvian, Chinese, Cuban and Mexican heritage shapes the menu. The Baja fish taco is the star: lightly battered fish with slaw, crema, radish and lime on corn tortillas. Chicharrón de pollo, Cubano sandwiches and yuca fries with ají amarillo round out the menu. Ordering is fast-casual in a bright, tropical-themed space. Catering and online ordering are also available.

Domenico's Italian Deli is a three-generation family institution on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. Its roots go back to 1966, when Dominic "Domenico" Cucchiara and his Italian-born wife Letizia bought the P&G Italian Delicatessen. The shop took the name Domenico's in 1982, and their daughter Ann Murphy has run it since 1989, with the next generation working behind the counter. The deli makes around 40 sandwiches with house-roasted turkey, hot coppa and hand-rolled meatballs. It also offers made-to-order pasta, and cannoli and cheesecake from family recipes. Open Monday through Saturday.
Verify Before Publishing: No official website found. Phone not confirmed on a fetched page.

Directory Description: Dragon Rouge Bistro is a waterfront Vietnamese restaurant on Blanding Avenue, along Alameda's northern shoreline. Its contemporary dining room and outdoor seating look out toward the bridge. Favorites include garlic noodles, "bouncing" beef tenderloin, pineapple fried rice and a crispy dragon's nest with prawns. The full bar pours craft cocktails, and daily happy hour pricing makes it a lively after-work stop. The restaurant is open every day for lunch and dinner, and also offers private dining, catering, takeout and delivery.

East End is an independent, locally owned restaurant inside The Marketplace on Park Street. Since 2011 it has made wood-fired pizza from a native-yeast sourdough, and the menu has since grown to include oysters shucked to order, craft cocktails and seasonal comfort dishes. The kitchen buys from local, responsible producers. East End serves dinner Tuesday through Saturday. Its daily 5–6 pm happy hour takes a dollar off house cocktails, draft beer and wine, and offers a dozen oysters for $12. Guests can dine in, order ahead for pickup, or get delivery.

East Ocean Seafood Restaurant on Webster Street has been a gathering place for the East Bay community for more than thirty years. The Cantonese-style restaurant serves dim sum at midday every day and Chinese seafood dishes at dinner. It has a full bar and dedicated banquet and wedding menus, so it is a common choice for family celebrations and large parties. Guests can reserve a table, order online for takeout, arrange catering, or buy frozen items to cook at home. Weekend dim sum starts at 9:30 am.

Fikscue serves what it calls Indo-Tex barbecue, pairing Texas-style smoked meats with Indonesian flavors. Co-owners Fik and Reka Saleh began with backyard barbecue and a pop-up selling Indonesian cookies, then opened on Park Street in November 2023. Everything on the menu is certified halal and pork-free. The menu runs from smoked brisket, beef ribs and house-made beef sausage to smoke-fried chicken and a brisket rendang plate served with rice, sambal and a spicy egg. In 2024, The New York Times named Fikscue one of the 50 best restaurants in the United States. The meats are slow-smoked, and popular items can sell out.
Verify Before Publishing: Current hours not verified (was weekends-only in 2024).

Directory Description: Fowl + Fare, on Santa Clara Avenue, specializes in fried chicken sandwiches and fried chicken biscuits known for their crisp crust and well-seasoned spice blends. It is a small, order-focused shop. Items often sell out, so ordering ahead through its online store is encouraged, and pickup and delivery are also available. Fowl + Fare is open for lunch and dinner Wednesday through Sunday, and closes early if it sells out.
Verify Before Publishing: Phone conflict: Downtown Alameda directory lists 510-630-5174.

Directory Description: Genghis Khan Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. According to the Downtown Alameda Business Association, its specialties include Mongolian barbecue and all-you-can-eat sushi, served alongside a budget-friendly Chinese buffet and lunch specials. The large dining room suits groups and families, and the restaurant is known for quick, friendly service.
Verify Before Publishing: Buffet / all-you-can-eat sushi details come from a directory listing that may be outdated — confirm.

Directory Description: Hang Ten Boiler combines Hawaiian comfort food with the messy fun of a seafood boil. Bay Area natives Paul and Mai Wong opened it on Santa Clara Avenue in November 2006 to bring the warmth and generous portions of Hawaiian cooking to Alameda. Plate-lunch favorites such as Lava Chicken, the BBQ Mixed Plate and Northshore Garlic Shrimp share the menu with seafood combos of king crab legs, shrimp, clams and corn, along with garlic noodles and kalua pork fries. The restaurant is open 11 am to 9 pm every day and offers dine-in, pickup, delivery, catering and happy hour specials.

Homeskillet is a family-owned breakfast and lunch spot on Park Street. It is known for donuts made by hand in-house, and alongside them it serves a full menu of hearty, traditional American breakfast and lunch dishes, with plates built around applewood-smoked bacon and fresh hash browns. Diners can stop in for a sit-down breakfast, pick up a box of donuts to go, or order pickup and delivery online.
Verify Before Publishing: Website titled 'Alameda Donuts and skillet' — possible rebrand. Hours/owners not found.

Directory Description: Hong Kong City is a Chinese restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. It is listed in the Downtown Alameda business directory as Hong Kong City Seafood Restaurant, and seafood is the focus. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup and delivery. It sits in the heart of the Park Street business district, an easy stop for lunch or dinner downtown. Hours vary by day, so check current hours before visiting.
Verify Before Publishing: Limited info. Name varies (Hong Kong City Seafood Restaurant / Hong Kong City Cafe); several websites.

Directory Description: Island Taqueria is a casual Mexican taqueria on Park Street in downtown Alameda. The menu covers the taqueria staples: street tacos topped with onions and cilantro, regular and "super" burritos with rice, beans, pico de gallo, guacamole and cheese, loaded super nachos, and combination plates and antojitos. Tortilla chips are cut and fried in-house every day. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup and delivery, which makes it an easy choice for a quick lunch or an early dinner downtown.
Verify Before Publishing: Limited info (menu only). No official website; phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Jim's Coffee Shop has been a family-run fixture in Alameda since 1960. Dimitris "Jim" Geanekos, an immigrant from Greece, opened it as a small takeout counter, and it later grew into a full-service restaurant. Today his son Tom runs the coffee shop, along with the sister location Jim's on the Course. The diner on Lincoln Avenue, just off Park Street, serves classic breakfast and lunch seven days a week from 7am to 3pm. The menu runs from omelets and eggs florentine to lunch plates such as fettuccine alfredo and salmon. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup, and large parties can reserve by phone.

La Penca Azul has served Mexican food on Park Street for more than 25 years, in the heart of Alameda's historic downtown near the Alameda Theatre. The menu covers tacos, burritos, quesadillas and enchiladas, with favorites such as carnitas, birria tacos and the oversized Super Famoso Burrito, and churros for dessert. Breakfast plates like huevos rancheros and chilaquiles are also on offer. A full bar pours signature margaritas, including peach and mango, from a selection of top-shelf tequilas. Diners can eat in, take out, order delivery or curbside pickup, or book catering. Sister locations operate elsewhere in Alameda and in Oakland.

Leña is a family-run modern Mexican restaurant on Central Avenue. Its motto is "Fire from our heritage", and the name is Spanish for firewood. Yesenia Chavez runs it with her family. Her parents come from Guanajuato, her brother-in-law leads the kitchen and her brother is sous chef. The menu offers elevated takes on traditional recipes from across Mexico, including halibut tacos, poblano enmolado, mole with Cornish game hen, oxtail and short rib birria, and whole achiote-marinated branzino. A lineup of seven signature tacos can also be ordered together. Leña serves dinner Tuesday through Sunday and brunch on weekends, and reservations are available online.

Mango & Mint is a fast-casual Vietnamese eatery on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. Owner Loan Nguyen opened it in March 2024, after running a cafe in Oakland for a decade. Guests order at the counter and build their meal from fresh ingredients on display behind the glass. The menu covers bánh mì (lemongrass pork is a favorite), vermicelli noodle bowls, rice plates, fresh spring rolls, crispy egg rolls and salads. Smoothies and Vietnamese coffee and tea round out the menu. There is limited indoor seating with a few outdoor tables, and takeout is available.
Verify Before Publishing: No official website; phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Moxie Steak House opened on Park Street in 2024 with chef Donna Meadows in the kitchen. Meadows is a longtime Alameda food figure who managed Little House Cafe for 15 years and once owned Boniere Bakery. The dining room mixes contemporary style with a speakeasy feel: emerald-green walls, gold accents, velvet chairs, and a full bar stocked to the ceiling. The à la carte menu features filet mignon, New York strip, grass-fed ribeye and lamb chops, with seasonal sauces and a slow-cooked veal demi-glace. Sides include hasselback potatoes and chive fritters. Moxie serves dinner Wednesday through Sunday and brunch on weekends, and takes reservations online.
Verify Before Publishing: Phone not confirmed; sources differ on who owns it (description names only the chef).

Directory Description: Pasta Pelican sits at the water's edge in Mariner Square, with views across the Oakland–Alameda Estuary to Jack London Square. The kitchen serves traditional Italian and American fare made with prime cuts, free-range chicken and organic produce. The menu runs from fettuccine alfredo, Bolognese and seafood ravioli to the house Pollo Pelicano and steaks such as filet mignon and New York strip. Lunch and dinner are served daily, and happy hour runs Friday through Sunday afternoons. An upstairs banquet room with waterfront views holds private events for 40 to 100 guests. Reservations are available online.

Peak is a women-owned restaurant on Webster Street that pairs two menus under one roof: brunch by day and Thai fusion by night. Mornings bring house-baked sourdough, brioche and croissants alongside pancakes, waffles, Benedicts, savory toasts and French toast. The signature dish is brioche toast with pandan cream, which draws on both halves of the menu. In the evening the kitchen turns to Thai-inspired plates built on family recipes, served with desserts and handcrafted cocktails. The dining room is cozy and decorated with art and handmade touches. Reservations and online ordering are both available. Peak is closed on Wednesdays.

Phnom Penh House serves Cambodian cooking on Webster Street. It started in Oakland before moving to Alameda. The menu is built for sharing, with entrees that balance smoky, salty and sweet flavors. A popular choice is traop ang: grilled eggplant topped with savory ground pork, shrimp and a generous amount of garlic. The dining room is relaxed and casual, which makes it an easy choice for a walk-in lunch or a weeknight dinner.
Verify Before Publishing: Limited info; phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Pizzeria Pappo is chef John Thiel's casual West End follow-up to Pappo, the sit-down restaurant he ran in Alameda for many years. Thiel trained at the California Culinary Academy and cooked at Bay Wolf. Here he makes two styles of pizza: East Coast thin crust sold by the slice or whole pie, and thick, rectangular Sicilian pies. The menu also includes panini, meatballs, pastas, garlic knots, focaccia and parmigiana plates, with a few favorites like fried olives carried over from the original restaurant. Italian wines and local craft beers are on offer, and there is ice cream for dessert. It is a relaxed, family-friendly spot and handles plenty of takeout.
Verify Before Publishing: Phone and current hours not confirmed.

Directory Description: Rose's Sandwich Shop is a Webster Street deli counter focused on hearty, made-to-order sandwiches. Turkey roasted in-house anchors much of the menu. It appears in the Classic with tomato and Swiss, and in the Giant, which stacks on avocado, cranberry, bacon and jack cheese. Fans of cured meats can order the Italian, layered with mortadella, ham, bologna and salami. Chicken salad, vegetarian choices and side salads round out the menu. Rose's is open daily from mid-morning into the early evening and is well suited to a quick lunch or takeout, with delivery available through the usual apps.
Verify Before Publishing: Menu-only detail; no owner/history found. Phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Saltbreaker is a neighborhood bistro at Alameda Point that serves California cooking grounded in French technique, built around seasonal produce from local farms. Chef Justin Davis's dinner menu moves from small plates such as smoked trout rillette and beef tartare to larger dishes like Ora King salmon and steak frites. A full cocktail program accompanies the food. Soon after opening, Eater SF named it one of the East Bay's hottest new restaurants. Next door, The Yard offers a more casual daytime option: a breezy patio with a full bar, oysters, chowder, fish and chips, smash burgers and a kids' menu.

Scolari's Good Eats has been serving comfort food on Park Street since 2010. It was opened by Dan Nichols, who also owns The Lucky 13 bar next door, together with executive chef Mike Boyd. The menu has an East Coast accent: burgers and fries, a Taylor ham, egg and cheese on brioche, and strombolis. House-made bread, daily pizza specials, a rotating list of specials and vegan options fill out the rest. Alameda Magazine gave its burger and fries top honors in 2012, the same year the team added a vintage 1964 Airstream food truck. The truck is now available for catering, and food can also be delivered to patrons at the Lucky 13.

Southern Comfort Kitchen brings New Orleans–style Cajun and Creole cooking to Webster Street. It is run by brothers Brett, Jason and Jeremy Brill, whose family spent 15 years as food vendors at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival. After moving to California, the family cooked at festivals, then ran food trucks, then opened restaurants in Castro Valley and Pleasant Hill before coming to Alameda in 2024. The menu covers the classics: po'boys with shrimp, catfish, oyster or soft-shell crab, jambalaya, seafood gumbo, crawfish étouffée, and blackened shrimp and grits. Service is fast-casual, with dine-in, takeout, delivery and a drive-through.
Verify Before Publishing: Phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: Southie brings East Coast-inspired, elevated American fare to Park Station, the beer venue at 1200 Park Street in downtown Alameda. This is the second location of Southie, from restaurateur Rich Wood, who also owns Oakland's Wood Tavern and The Wolf. The kitchen keeps a seasonal menu that changes often, with sandwiches and shareable bites made to go with Park Station's drinks. Guests order the food and drinks together in a relaxed, social setting that suits a casual lunch, a game-day gathering or an evening out with friends. Online ordering is available for pickup.
Verify Before Publishing: Your list's number (510-671-2903) is Park Station's; Southie's own line is 510-696-4247.

Directory Description: Since 2002, Speisekammer has served traditional German cooking on Lincoln Avenue in Alameda. Chef Peter Kahl, a native of Flensburg, Germany, runs the kitchen, where hearty classics share the menu with rotating seasonal specials, and many dishes come in regular or smaller portions. The bar pours 16 beers on tap, from German imports to local craft brews. Guests can eat in the dining room or in the outdoor beer garden, where dogs are welcome. Live music on many evenings, with no cover charge, adds to the gemütlich atmosphere.

Spinning Bones is a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand–recognized rotisserie on Park Street that blends California cooking with Japanese flavors. Owners Mike Yakura and Danny Sterling opened it in 2019. Meats such as chicken, black pepper tri-tip and pork shoulder are marinated in shio koji and roasted on spits, then served with bright sauces like chimichurri and garlic-jalapeño garum. Starters include mochiko fried chicken nuggets and cauliflower with miso butter and furikake. The room is relaxed and neighborhood-friendly, and there's outdoor seating plus beer, wine and sake to round out a meal.

Tahina Fresh Mediterranean is a counter-service spot inside the Alameda Marketplace on Park Street. Rumtin Rahmani, longtime owner of The Beanery in the same marketplace, opened it with his sister Talayeh and partner Rochelle Nasab. The menu centers on herb-forward, house-made falafel in soft pita, alongside chicken shawarma, mezze plates and cilantro hummus. California touches include quinoa tabouli with avocado and saffron rice. Moroccan mint tea, pomegranate lemonade and baklava finish the meal. It's an easy choice for a quick lunch or an early dinner, and online ordering is available.
Verify Before Publishing: Sunday hours conflict between website and Marketplace page.

Directory Description: The Bureau 510 is the West Alameda outpost of an Emeryville gastropub, open on Webster Street since 2023. Owner Chalit Sangsana's menu mixes international street food with comfort classics. Burgers come with crispy fries, sometimes stacked right on top, and share the menu with banh mi, fish tacos and Korean-style short ribs. The industrial-chic space serves lunch and dinner with beer and cocktails. Happy hour runs in the late afternoon, making it an easy stop after work on the Webster Street corridor.
Verify Before Publishing: Newest listing found is May 2026 — confirm still open. No website; phone not confirmed.

Directory Description: The Hobnob is a casual, friendly neighborhood restaurant and bar in downtown Alameda, serving California comfort food made with seasonal ingredients. Dinner might start with ricotta beignets or buffalo cauliflower and move on to a Nashville spicy fried chicken sandwich, a diner burger, pan-seared salmon or a flat iron steak. Craft cocktails, beer and wine are available throughout. On weekends, brunch brings pancakes, omelets, French toast and eggs Benedict. Friday nights turn lively with karaoke, and the restaurant also offers private party space and catering.

Trabocco Kitchen and Cocktails has brought the flavors of Abruzzo to Alameda's South Shore Center since 2013. Chef-owner Giuseppe Naccarelli grew up in the Italian region and named his restaurant after the trabocchi, the wooden fishing huts along its Adriatic coast, echoed by a net installation above the dining room. The menu leans toward coastal cooking, including salt cod, octopus and brodetto alla vastese seafood stew, alongside handmade pasta with rabbit ragù, oxtail ravioli and rotisserie rabbit. A full cocktail program makes it a good fit for anything from lunch to a celebratory dinner.

Waki is a Japanese restaurant on Webster Street in West Alameda focused on sushi and carefully prepared Japanese dishes. The menu runs from bluefin tuna tataki and hamachi carpaccio to signature rolls such as the dragon roll, along with cooked favorites like beef and salmon teriyaki. For a broader sampling, there's the "Waki's Tasting" option. Wine and beer are served. Waki is open for dinner nightly and for lunch on Sundays, and it also offers takeout ordering, catering and private parties for larger groups.
Verify Before Publishing: Recently under new management per its website.

Directory Description: Wild Ginger serves Chinese street food on Park Street in downtown Alameda, with a menu built around noodles. Wide, chewy biang biang hand-pulled noodles and cumin lamb noodles sit alongside hearty beef noodle soup, cold noodles and malatang. Other favorites include rou jia mo, a lamb "burger" on griddled bread, spicy tingly beef, and sour and spicy pork dumplings. The kitchen emphasizes fresh ingredients and carefully balanced seasoning. There's indoor and outdoor seating, and it's open for lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday, with online ordering for takeout.
